No bullfighting in Japan; found in Spain, Portugal and Latin America.

No bridge or tower bungee site was found inside the metro area; the nearest operator sites are Ryujin Gorge in Ibaraki (about 2 to 2.5 hours) and Minakami/Sarugakyo in Gunma (about 3 hours by train), run by Bungy Japan.
Needs gorges; Canyons Okutama runs tours in west Tokyo about 90 minutes from the centre.
No flooded cave systems near Tokyo; the nearest cave diving is in Okinawa and Shikoku.
Limestone caves such as Nippara Cave are in the Okutama mountains, around 2 hours from central Tokyo.
Needs snow and sled-dog culture; nearest is Hokkaido.
Japan has no accessible glaciers for trekking; nearest alternatives are in the Alps or New Zealand.
Forest Adventure Yokohama has a family-friendly tree-top trek course with suspension bridges and rope ladders, plus a trampoline net course.
FlyStation Japan in Koshigaya, Saitama has a 20 m transparent wind tunnel with first-flight and flight-school plans (2019 source).

No indoor snow slope operates in central Tokyo (the Funabashi ski dome closed), but Sayama Ski Resort in Saitama has a 300 m indoor slope about 40-60 minutes by train and Snova Shin-Yokohama has a 60 m slope.
Needs a purpose-built track; none in the Tokyo area.
Alpine mountaineering means the Japanese Alps, around 3 hours away; Okutama peaks are hiking terrain.
Tokyo Skydiving Club at Honda Airport in Saitama offers tandem jumps and AFF, about 40 km north of Tokyo (beyond the metro radius).
Needs launch slopes; the nearest schools are around Mt Tsukuba and the Fuji foothills, 1.5 to 2 hours away.
No rodeo tradition in Japan; found in North America, Australia and parts of Latin America.
No free-roaming wildlife to see; nearest equivalent is drive-through safari parks, about 2 hours away.
No dunes near Tokyo; the Tottori Sand Dunes are far to the west.
No true ski simulator was found, but Tokyo-area indoor real-snow slopes exist: Snova Shin-Yokohama (60 m slope with rails and half-pipe) and Sayama Ski Resort in Saitama (300 m indoor slope).
No natural snow in Tokyo; the nearest ski resorts (e.g. Gala Yuzawa) are about 90 minutes away by Shinkansen.
Volcano boarding is done on Cerro Negro in Nicaragua; no equivalent in Japan.
Rafting needs rapids; the Tama River in Okutama (about 1.5 hours away) and Tone River in Gunma are the nearest.
Forest Adventure Yokohama's trek course includes zip lines among its tree-top obstacles; Forest Adventure Chiba and Tokyo Snow Club guided trips offer more.
